title: Methods, Virology & More
text:
Welcome! On this site, I will post a blog as well as files related to my personal interests, my work as a virologist, and thoughts about the quantitative methods applied to medical science.
Over the fifty + years I’ve been working with quantitative methods, I’ve seen some very interesting applications, especially now that I work as a virologist at the Retrovirology Laboratory of UNIFESP (Federal University of São Paulo). Many of these applications relate to the sequencing the genome (the entire range of DNA) of organisms and viruses, or anything coded by DNA.
I also run across a lot of abuse of simple statistics in papers, talks, and opinions in all media. I will try to use some of this space to set some of these misapprehensions back on the right path.
This site is still in an experimental stage and will hopefully take on a more professional appearance in the coming weeks.
As an important footnote, I am an American who has moved definitively to Brazil. I won’t be able to be silent over some issues of cultural, political and all other types of differences between these two cultures. There will also be some posts in Portuguese, and others that I want both Americans and Brazilians to read that I will post in both languages.

title: First Post to the New Blog
text:
It has been a while since I last blogged. I have moved from being an urban planner and real estate consultant to applying my quantitative skills to virology and medical science. I have managed to achieve my long-held goal of completing a doctorate and I have been conducting research on HIV and other viral diseases as well as teaching biomedical and other students at the Federal University of São Paulo.
My focus remains quantitative methods, especially biostatistics, bioinformatics, and the computer programming necessary to answer fundamental–and sometimes trivial–questions related to disease. I teach annually a short course on using the computer language R to conduct medical research.
I’ve also had the privilege of consulting for a number of biotech companies in Brazil, the United States and Israel on research and drug development. Again, my focus is on the quantitative aspects of the research, although my decade of study of viruses, how they function and how to combat the diseases they cause form a large part of what I contribute to these research efforts.

title: First Post to the New Blog
section: What This Blog Will Be About
text:
What This Blog Will Be About
I would like to address three principal areas in this blog.

What I am thinking about and working on related to the medical research projects that our laboratory is dealing with. There are many topics that come up that are not really germane to the academic publications that scientists use as their primary means of communications, but may be of interest to individuals and groups outside our team.
Issues in biostatistics, probability and other subjects related to quantitative methods. These will include guides to understanding specific issues in statistical decision-making, use and abuse of statistical models, methods and tests, and general comments on mathematics. I will always try to keep the explanations I offer here understandable without requiring a Ph.D. just to read the blog.
Related to the quantitative techniques themselves, the computer languages and software we use to study biological data create many issues that are worthy of discussion. Although I have been a person who uses the R language to conduct analyses for the last fifteen years, I will also explore the use of other languages such as Python and Julia with which I am familiar. However, I promise there will be no posts on the R vs Python theme. I will also address from time to time the use of large, canned statistical analysis programs such as SPSS, Stata, Prism, etc.

title: First Post to the New Blog
text:
Other Interests
While these three areas will be my primary focus, I am also interested in world politics, especially in the Middle East, in my home country (USA) and in Latin America. If I feel that I have something original to contribute on these topics, I will. I also am deeply interested in music, literature and art, so these areas will not totally escape my attention here.
I will continue to develop the structure of the blog, which is being written and structured in the Quarto markdown system via the new IDE called Positron (link to Positron IDE) and I will soon add a comments capability – as soon as I figure out how.
Any topics you would like me to address, please let me know. The blog has a number of links you can use to reach me.
